subject: english-language
title: Reading Between the Lines
welcome_lead: Some meaning is on the page; some you must dig out.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on explicit and implicit meaning.
final_note: You can now tell explicit from implicit information in a text.

concepts.def: Reasoning from clues to a conclusion.
Text used to back up a reading.
Small detail you can use as evidence.
Your reading of the text's meaning.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Tom slammed the door' is explicit about an action; the anger behind it is implicit — we infer it.
Inference = reading between the lines. Use small clues to reach a fair conclusion the writer hasn't spelt out.
Always anchor inference in evidence — a quote or detail from the text. Without evidence, it's guesswork.

mcqs.q: Stated directly on the page is.

numericals.q: How many terms here (explicit, implicit, inference, evidence, clue, interpretation)?

free_texts.q: A meaning hinted at but not stated outright is ____.
